applies_why: The judge text assigns UNDERDETERMINED to a single-verse link while relying on the verse/word evidence cutting both ways, which is what K-S2 governs.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- the sign's chapter bounds (Isaiah 7:16; 8:3-4; 8:8) are real, but C5's own narrowing concedes Matthew 1:23's application stands, and the almah/bethulah word-count cuts both ways (Joel 1:8); answered in [CR2] section G and [CR3] LINK 5.
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand': (a) any dual-sense or both-ways word evidence cannot yield UNDERDETERMINED because both senses stand; (b) it only bars calling a verse open while allowing UNDERDETERMINED on other grounds.
why: The judge marks the link UNDERDETERMINED even while saying the chapter bounds are real and Matthew 1:23's application stands, treating the two-sided evidence as unresolved contrary to K-S2's command that a two-sense verse is not open and both senses stand.
